stories.headline: Zelensky says Starshield speed cap is back, crippling Ukraine's interceptors against jet-powered drones

key_facts.fact: On Nov. 12 Zelensky said Ukraine's military had faced significant Starshield disruptions for several days, with systematic restrictions capping the service at 161 km/h (100 mph).
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine's military is once again experiencing significant disruptions to the Starshield satellite communications system, the militarized version of Starlink, for several days, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Nov. 12. Restrictions limit Starshield's operating speed to 161 kilometers per hour (100 miles per hour)

key_facts.fact: Zelensky said the limits affect the entire front line and occupied territories, and some Russian strikes got through because interceptors could not reach the needed speed.
key_facts.excerpt: "Unfortunately, there have already been strikes that got through because our interception systems cannot reach sufficient speeds and are unable to intercept in time."

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's military investigated and concluded the disruptions were systematic restrictions, not random technical errors; Kyiv is trying to establish the circumstances with the US side.
key_facts.excerpt: He said Ukraine's military had investigated the disruptions and concluded they were not random technical errors but systematic restrictions. ... "We are trying to establish all the circumstances with the American side," he added.

key_facts.fact: The new cap comes less than three weeks after Ukraine's Defence Ministry said on Oct. 24 that connectivity had been restored at speeds above 400 km/h, following a first cap recorded on Oct. 13-14.
key_facts.excerpt: On 24 October, Ukraine's Defence Ministry confirmed that connectivity had been restored, with stable connections at speeds exceeding 400 kilometres per hour. The restrictions were first recorded overnight on 13–14 October

key_facts.fact: Responsibility is disputed: Trump denied ordering the October slowdown, while Musk wrote that Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump denied ordering the slowdown at the time, while US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the administration was not responsible. SpaceX chief executive Elon Musk said ... "Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government."

key_facts.fact: Presidential adviser Serhii Beskrestnov said the cap disrupted links with helicopters tracking Shahed-type drones and with jet interceptors.
key_facts.excerpt: problems have arisen with communication with the helicopters tracking the Shahed-type drones and with the jet interceptors shooting down the jet-powered drones.

key_facts.fact: The FT reported the restrictions returned as US envoys landed in Moscow for talks with Putin.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine says Starlink restrictions are back as US envoys land in Moscow ... hampering efforts to intercept Russian drones as US diplomatic efforts continu...

stories.headline: Iran claims mine strike on tanker in Hormuz as Israel readies for possible attack and Vance weighs talks

key_facts.fact: On Nov. 11 Iran's army said a 'violating' oil tanker caught fire after striking a naval mine in a prohibited area east of the Strait of Hormuz; a Saudi-flagged tanker, NCC Fajr, was involved in a 'possible attack' the same day.
key_facts.excerpt: On Wednesday Iran's army said, via state television, that "a violating oil tanker caught fire after striking a naval mine" in an "unsafe, prohibited area" in the east of the strait. ... Also on Wednesday, a Saudi-flagged tanker, the NCC Fajr, was involved in a "possible attack" in the strait

key_facts.fact: At least 10 ships were hit in the first ten days of November after 37 attacks in October; the IMO has confirmed 133 incidents and at least 25 seafarers killed since the war began.
key_facts.excerpt: At least 10 ships were hit in the first ten days of November, after 37 attacks in October, the highest monthly tally since the war began in late February ... the International Maritime Organization has confirmed 133 incidents and at least 25 seafarers killed.

key_facts.fact: Reuters sources confirmed Iran attacked ship navigation systems on Oman's Didamar island in the strait, infrastructure used to restore Gulf oil flows.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran has attacked ship navigation systems on the Omani island of Didamar in the Strait of Hormuz, three sources with knowledge of the matter confirmed, showing Tehran's ability to target infrastructure used to restore Gulf oil flows.

key_facts.fact: Israel's security cabinet instructed the military to step up preparations for a possible attack on Iran, public broadcaster KAN reported on Nov. 11.
key_facts.excerpt: Israel's security cabinet has instructed the military to step up preparations for a possible attack on Iran, Israeli public broadcaster KAN reported Wednesday evening.

key_facts.fact: Vice President JD Vance is considering face-to-face talks with Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei, and Trump has empowered him to negotiate, the WSJ reported; officials called the discussions preliminary.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. Vice President JD Vance is considering face-to-face talks with Iranian Security Chief Mohsen Rezaei, sources told the Wall Street Journal. ... President Trump has told top aides and counterparts he's open to Vance reopening talks with Iran and has empowered Vance to negotiate.

key_facts.fact: Saudi air defences intercepted Houthi missiles and drones aimed at Riyadh, Mecca and other regions on Nov. 11; debris from two ballistic missiles fell in the Mecca region.
key_facts.excerpt: Saudi air defences intercepted Houthi missiles and drones launched towards Riyadh, Mecca and other regions on Wednesday, as hostilities between the Iran-aligned group and the kingdom worsen.

key_facts.fact: January Brent fell 1.6% to $91.3 a barrel on Thursday after the report that Vance was considering direct talks with Iran.
key_facts.excerpt: January-delivery Brent crude oil fell 1.6% to $91.3 a barrel after US Vice President JD Vance reportedly considered direct talks with Maj. Gen. Mohsen Rezaei

stories.headline: Beijing tells US to stop 'spy narrative' tech curbs and rebukes G7 on Taiwan ahead of Trump-Xi summit

key_facts.fact: At a Nov. 12 briefing, foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said the US should stop fabricating the 'so-called Chinese spy narrative' as a pretext for imposing technology restrictions.
key_facts.excerpt: China has urged the United States to stop "fabricating so-called spy narratives and using them as a pretext for imposing a technological blockade" ... Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning made the comments at a press briefing on Thursday

key_facts.fact: Mao said China and the US remain in close communication on leader-level interactions and Beijing is ready to implement the consensus reached by the two presidents; Trump and Xi meet next week at APEC in Shenzhen.
key_facts.excerpt: The remarks come ahead of a meeting next week between Trump and Xi at the APEC gathering in Shenzhen, southern China.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg noted the summit comes with less than two months left on the US-China trade ceasefire, and that Washington lawmakers have called for tighter tech restrictions since the spy allegations surfaced.
key_facts.excerpt: The scandal surrounding Huang is complicating a meeting next week between Chinese leader Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump – a summit that comes with less than two months remaining on a trade ceasefire.

key_facts.fact: Asked about a possible China-Russia-US leaders' meeting in Shenzhen, Mao said China is maintaining communication with relevant parties and will release information in a timely manner.
key_facts.excerpt: "China is maintaining communication with relevant parties regarding the meeting between the Chinese, Russian, and US leaders. We will release further information in a timely manner if there is any."

key_facts.fact: G7 foreign ministers said on Nov. 11 that China's assertive actions in waters east of Taiwan threaten regional stability; China's foreign ministry said the statement 'crudely interferes in China's internal affairs.'
key_facts.excerpt: G7 foreign ministers last night released a joint declaration that China's increasingly assertive actions in the waters east of Taiwan threaten regional stability and freedom of navigation. ... China's Foreign Ministry today said the statement "disregards objective facts… crudely interferes in China's internal affairs"

key_facts.fact: Taiwan President Lai Ching-te said on Nov. 12 that Taiwan is taking part in the APEC leaders' summit in Shenzhen on an 'equal basis', after Taipei sought a written guarantee from Beijing.
key_facts.excerpt: Taiwan is participating in this year's APEC leaders' summit in China on the principle of interaction on an "equal basis", President Lai Ching-te said on Thursday, after his government called for a written guarantee from Beijing for that to happen.

stories.headline: Trump threatens to 'immediately' double tariffs on Mexico unless it stops migrant caravans

key_facts.fact: In a Truth Social post on Thursday morning, Nov. 12, Trump wrote that if Mexico does not stop migrant caravans, 'the Tariffs on Mexico will be IMMEDIATELY DOUBLED.'
key_facts.excerpt: "MEXICO MUST STOP THEM, NOW, and if they do not do so, the Tariffs on Mexico will be IMMEDIATELY DOUBLED," he added.

key_facts.fact: Trump tied the caravans to the midterm results, writing that with 'the perceived loss by the Republicans in the Midterms' the 'INVASION of our Country is taking place again.'
key_facts.excerpt: "Here we go again!" Trump began a lengthy post on Truth Social. "With the perceived loss by the Republicans in the Midterms – I WAS NOT ON THE BALLOT- the INVASION of our Country is taking place again."

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg described the move as ratcheting up trade tensions with a major economic partner.
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump threatened to double tariffs on goods from Mexico "immediately" if the country did not stop what he claimed were migrant caravans preparing to head to the US, ratcheting up trade tensions with a major economic partner.

key_facts.fact: President Claudia Sheinbaum said two caravans are crossing southern Mexico, one shrunk from about 600 people to about 100 and another of about 1,500, and that no caravan has reached the US border since Trump took office.
key_facts.excerpt: Sheinbaum said there are currently two caravans, one that started in the southern Mexican state of Chiapas with around 600 people but has decreased to about a hundred, and another with mostly Hondurans. This caravan consists of around 1,500 people.

key_facts.fact: Current US tariffs on Mexico include 25% on passenger vehicles and light trucks, 50% on steel, aluminum and copper, and 25% on goods that don't meet USMCA rules of origin.
key_facts.excerpt: Current Trump tariffs on Mexico include 25% tariffs on imported passenger vehicles and light trucks, a 50% tariff on steel, aluminum and copper, and 17% tariff on tomatoes. Goods that do not meet rules-of-origin requirements under the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement are also subject to 25% tariffs.

key_facts.fact: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the caravan 'will NOT be allowed to enter our country.'
key_facts.excerpt: "We will utilize all assets to make sure our borders are secure," he wrote on social media Thursday. "This illegal migrant caravan will NOT be allowed to enter our country. Full stop."

key_facts.excerpt: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow on Thursday for talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin ... Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev met the two American representatives at Vnukovo Airport

key_facts.fact: After meeting Putin, the envoys are due to go to Ireland to meet Zelensky; the Abu Dhabi talks ended with a large prisoner-exchange deal but no visible breakthrough.

stories.headline: Reuters: FDA quietly shelves Makary's one-to-two-month priority voucher review program

key_facts.fact: The FDA has shelved the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher program launched in June 2025 by former commissioner Marty Makary, according to six sources and internal documents cited by Reuters.
key_facts.excerpt: No new drugs have been given a voucher under the FDA's fast-track review program since Marty Makary left the agency in May. According to internal documents and six sources familiar with the matter, the initiative has now been shelved.

key_facts.fact: The program aimed to compress drug review timelines to as little as one to two months for therapies addressing national priorities.
key_facts.excerpt: Its aim was to compress drug review timelines to as little as one to two months for therapies addressing national priorities, such as urgent unmet health needs.

key_facts.fact: Of 22 drugs given a voucher, 12 have been approved, including five since Makary's departure; for several drugs the program sped approval by eight months or more.
key_facts.excerpt: Of the 22 drugs given a voucher, a dozen have been approved, including five since Makary's departure. For several drugs, the program sped approval by eight months or more.

key_facts.fact: An executive council of political appointees that oversaw reviews has gone dormant; companies can still apply, but applications do not advance.
key_facts.excerpt: A key component of the scheme, an executive council of political appointees that oversaw drug reviews and had a central role in speeding approvals, has gone dormant ... FDA leadership told companies the agency is not moving forward with the program but is keeping applications open. When companies submit them, they don't advance

key_facts.fact: HHS spokesperson Emily Hilliard said the pilot is ongoing and the FDA is reviewing feedback from a June public hearing to refine the framework.
key_facts.excerpt: HHS spokesperson Emily Hilliard said the pilot is ongoing and that the FDA is reviewing feedback from a June public hearing on it to refine the framework.

key_facts.fact: Critics had argued the selection process was opaque, lacked statutory backing and might reward companies for pricing deals or domestic manufacturing pledges.
key_facts.excerpt: critics arguing that the selection process is opaque, the programme lacks statutory backing, and undermines usual FDA review process standards. ... recipients may be selected for political reasons – for example, as a quid pro quo for pricing deals announced by the Trump administration or investments in domestic manufacturing.

stories.headline: China approves Eli Lilly's orforglipron, its first GLP-1 weight-loss pill, beating Novo Nordisk

key_facts.fact: China approved Eli Lilly's oral GLP-1 orforglipron for weight management on Nov. 12, making Lilly the first drugmaker with a GLP-1 weight-loss pill approved in the country.
key_facts.excerpt: Eli Lilly became the first drugmaker to have a GLP-1 weight-loss pill approved in China, with the country clearing its oral candidate orforglipron for weight management (Reuters Biopharma, 2026-11-12).

key_facts.fact: The approval gives Lilly an edge over Novo Nordisk in the world's second-largest pharmaceutical market; Novo's oral Wegovy is not yet approved in China, and Lilly applied first.
key_facts.excerpt: The approval gives Lilly an advantage over Danish rival Novo Nordisk in the world's second-largest pharmaceutical market. ... Novo's oral version of Wegovy has not yet been approved in China. Lilly was first to apply with orforglipron.

key_facts.fact: The pill will compete with once-weekly GLP-1 injections from Novo Nordisk, Pfizer and local firm Innovent Biologics.
key_facts.excerpt: Orforglipron will compete for market share in China with once-weekly GLP-1 weight-loss injections from Novo Nordisk, Pfizer, and local firm Innovent Biologics.

key_facts.fact: China's National Health Commission has said the share of overweight or obese people could exceed 65% by 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: China's National Health Commission has said the rate of overweight or obese people could reach more than 65% by 2030.

key_facts.fact: Separately, Lilly struck a strategic partnership with Gedeon Richter gaining global rights to develop estetrol (E4) combinations, and will buy about $15 million of Richter shares.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the terms of the agreement, Lilly gains global rights to develop E4 combinations in women's health and cardiometabolic disease ... Lilly will acquire approximately $15 million of RICHT ordinary shares from treasury.
